issues.t: Fast brake pad and rotor wear
issues.sym: Squealing or grinding, a pulsing pedal, and pads and rotors that need replacing far sooner than expected.
issues.why: Owners of early Journeys widely report short brake life; calipers that stick or overheat make the wear worse.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at least once a year, and make sure caliper slides are cleaned and lubricated whenever pads are replaced.

issues.t: Ignition can switch off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off after a bump or jolt, taking away power steering, power brake assist and airbag readiness.
issues.why: The wireless ignition node and key could let the ignition slip out of the Run position.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall and have it completed. Use a light key ring with nothing hanging from the key until it is done.

issues.t: Engine computer can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: An adhesive used when building the engine computer could crack its circuit board.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall and have it done.

issues.t: Engine wiring can rub through and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, or electrical faults.
issues.why: An engine wiring harness could rub against the left transmission mount until it shorted.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for the recall. Stop driving if you smell burning wires or see smoke.

issues.t: Door wiring breaks and disables side airbags (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light; power windows, locks or mirrors on that door may also act up.
issues.why: The wiring harness that runs into the front door can break from repeated door opening, cutting the side-impact sensor signal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the harness repaired.

issues.t: Airbag control unit can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light on.
issues.why: The airbag control module could corrode, so airbags might not deploy in a crash or could go off unexpectedly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it done.

issues.t: Power steering pressure hose can leak and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Whining steering, fluid under the front, a burning smell, or heavier steering.
issues.why: The high-pressure steering hose could pull loose at its crimped fitting and spray fluid on hot engine parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for the recall. Stop driving if you see smoke or smell burning fluid.

issues.t: Power steering hose can burst in cold weather (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden heavy steering soon after a cold start, with power steering fluid on the ground.
issues.why: The power steering return hose could split from high pressure when the fluid is very cold.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for the recall and have the hose replaced.

issues.t: Left cylinder head misfire (3.6L warranty extension)
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire codes on the left-side cylinders, a ticking noise, rough idle and lost power.
issues.why: Valve seat problems in the left cylinder head of early 3.6L engines cause low compression on those cylinders.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed promptly and ask a dealer whether the extended warranty still covers your vehicle.

issues.t: Oil filter housing and cooler leak (3.6L)
issues.sym: Oil or coolant pooling in the valley at the top-rear of the engine, drips under the car, a burning smell, or slowly dropping coolant.
issues.why: The plastic filter housing and oil cooler sit under the intake and warp or crack with heat, or their seals fail.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the housing replaced; many shops use an all-aluminum replacement. Watch the coolant level until it is fixed.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing failure (3.6L recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the bottom of the engine, low oil pressure warning, or the engine seizing.
issues.why: Debris left in some engines during manufacture could damage a connecting rod bearing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Stop driving if you hear knocking or see an oil pressure warning.

issues.t: Contaminated brake fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal or reduced braking.
issues.why: Brake fluid contaminated at the factory could damage rubber seals in the brake system.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for the recall and have it done before relying on the brakes.

issues.t: ABS and stability control quit in wet weather (recall)
issues.sym: ABS, traction control and stability control lights come on, often after rain or washing.
issues.why: Water can get into the ABS module wiring connector and short it, shutting off anti-lock braking and stability control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Normal brakes still work, but allow extra stopping distance on wet roads until it is fixed.

issues.t: 2.4L engine cover can fall onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The plastic engine cover can come loose and rest on the hot exhaust manifold.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall. Stop and check under the hood if you smell burning plastic.

issues.t: Driver airbag wiring can chafe (recall)
issues.sym: Airbag warning light, or in rare cases the driver airbag deploys without a crash.
issues.why: Wiring inside the steering wheel can rub through and short.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it done.

issues.t: False low oil pressure code (3.6L)
issues.sym: Check engine light with an oil pressure sensor code while the engine otherwise runs normally.
issues.why: The oil pressure sensor can fail and report a fault that is not really there.
issues.next: Have the oil level and actual oil pressure checked first; if both are fine, the bulletin calls for a new sensor.

issues.t: Cruise control may not disengage (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control keeps holding or raising speed after you try to cancel it.
issues.why: If certain wiring shorts, a software flaw can keep cruise control active.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the fix is a software update. Avoid cruise control until it is done.

issues.t: Sudden loss of drive power (transmission pump recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle suddenly loses the ability to move under power.
issues.why: The transmission oil pump can seize and lose hydraulic pressure.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall and have it repaired.

issues.t: Crank or cam sensor can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or cuts out intermittently while driving.
issues.why: A faulty crankshaft or camshaft position sensor can drop its signal.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall and have the sensor replaced.

issues.t: Headlamp side reflector too dim (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing the driver notices; the amber side reflector in the headlamp is less visible to other drivers at night.
issues.why: The reflector does not meet brightness requirements.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it done at your next dealer visit.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper pistons may reduce braking (recall)
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances or a soft pedal feel.
issues.why: Rear caliper pistons may lack proper coating, letting gas pockets form in the caliper.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it done before relying on the brakes.

issues.t: Engine computer power chip can fail (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: A voltage regulator chip in the engine computer can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have it repaired.

issues.t: Backup camera image missing or distorted (recalls)
issues.sym: The rearview camera picture is slow to appear, cuts out, or looks garbled when in reverse.
issues.why: Camera software faults on 2018 models and a cracked processor in the display on later models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recalls and have them done. Check mirrors and look behind you until it is fixed.
